title: Masking Black Hole Spin with a Modified Chaplygin Gas Envelope: Radiative Degeneracies from a Phenomenological Three-Region Spacetime
summary: Theoretical interpretations of horizon-scale observations often rely on the idealized assumption of an isolated vacuum Kerr geometry. However, astrophysical black holes are expected to be embedded within dense dark matter distributions that can modify the local spacetime geometry. In this work, we propose a theoretical framework to model a rotating compact object surrounded by a bounded dark matter envelope governed by a Modified Chaplygin Gas (MCG) equation of state.
